name: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
notes: This record covers the laboratory only as the host of the Bevatron and the antiproton experiment; other Berkeley Lab experiments belong to other streams.

Berkeley Lab History says the lab's legacy began in summer 1928, that the building later called the Rad Lab was committed to Lawrence on 26 August 1931, and that the University established the Radiation Laboratory as an independent entity on 1 July 1936; the founding interval uses 1931 at year precision.

summary.plain: The U.S. Department of Energy laboratory above Berkeley, California, that grew out of Ernest Lawrence's cyclotron laboratory of the 1930s. Its Bevatron accelerator, completed in 1954, produced the first antiprotons in 1955.
summary.technical: Managed by the University of California for the DOE; successor of the Radiation Laboratory founded around the cyclotron in 1931. Operated the 6.5 GeV Bevatron proton synchrotron (1954-1993), on which Chamberlain, Segrè, Wiegand and Ypsilantis observed antiprotons in 1955.
